query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small interstitial concentration (≈1 at. %) of boron to a Mn0.86Fe0.14NiSi alloy will (a) increase room-temperature fracture strain by ≥50 % while (b) lowering the peak isothermal magnetic-entropy change |ΔS_M| at Δµ₀H = 2 T by ≤10 %.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline Mn0.86Fe0.14NiSi alloy produced by arc melting and homogenisation, exhibiting a coupled magnetostructural transition (martensite↔austenite) near 300 K, with typical brittleness (fracture strain ≲0.5 %).
generation.intervention: Introduce 1 at.% B during melting, followed by identical homogenisation and a 850 °C/2 h anneal to ensure solid solubility and grain-boundary segregation.
generation.conditions: Measurements at 280–320 K under magnetic-field changes up to 2 T; polycrystalline bulk samples with comparable grain size (10–30 µm).
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregates to grain boundaries and forms nm-scale amorphous B-rich intergranular layers that (i) blunt and deflect martensite-induced cracks and (ii) slightly refine the grain size without altering the Laves-type crystal structure inside grains.
generation.mechanism: The intergranular B layers accommodate interfacial shear and volume misfit generated during the magnetostructural transformation, reducing stress concentration and impeding crack propagation; because B does not substitute in the magnetic sub-lattice, the Mn–Fe exchange interactions and density-of-states near the Fermi level (which govern |ΔS_M|) remain almost unchanged, preserving the large magnetocaloric response.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the undoped alloy, the B-doped material will show (1) tensile or compressive fracture strain ≥0.75 % (≥50 % higher) and a two- to three-fold increase in fracture toughness; (2) a peak |ΔS_M| still ≥20 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at Δµ₀H = 2 T (drop ≤10 %). Transformation temperature and hysteresis may shift by <5 K.
generation.baseline: Identical Mn0.86Fe0.14NiSi alloy fabricated without B addition and processed under the same thermal history.
generation.boundary: B content 0.5–2 at.% ; grain size 5–50 µm; measurements limited to Δµ₀H ≤2 T and 260–340 K. Outside these compositional or field limits, the trade-off between ductility and MCE may change.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of |ΔS_M| retention is inferred; if interstitial B unexpectedly perturbs electronic states or promotes secondary phases, the MCE drop could exceed 10 %. Grain-boundary chemistry after heat treatment is assumed but not yet confirmed.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches: (A) baseline Mn0.86Fe0.14NiSi and (B) Mn0.86Fe0.14NiSi0.99B0.01, both arc-melted, homogenised, and annealed identically. Machine cylindrical compression specimens and parallelepiped pieces for magnetisation tests.
measurements: Room-temperature compressive stress–strain curves to fracture
Temperature-dependent magnetisation M(T) at 0 and 2 T to derive |ΔS_M|(T) via the Maxwell relation
XRD and TEM/EDS of grain boundaries to verify B segregation and phase purity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if either (i) the average fracture strain (or K_IC) of batch B is ≤10 % greater than that of batch A, or (ii) the peak |ΔS_M| of batch B under Δµ₀H = 2 T is <90 % of batch A.
